newsitem.title: UK: BA declines to put value on its 168 slots.
newsitem.headline: BA declines to put value on its 168 slots.

text.p: British Airways on Sunday declined comment on newspaper reports that the 168 take-off and landing slots at Heathrow that it has to sell in order to merge with American Airlines would earn up to 800 million stg.
"We are not going to put a figure on it. All we have said is we want to get a fair market value for the slots," a spokeswoman told Reuters.

On Friday, President of the Board of Trade Ian Lang said the proposed link up between BA and AA would be referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission unless the two airlines agreed to make available 168 slots of their weekly allocation at Heathrow.
The Sunday Times said BA would earn 180 million stg from the sale of its first batch of the 168 slots. The paper derived the figure from the amount AA paid for slots in 1991.
The Sunday Telegraph said BA wanted 800 million stg for the full 168 slots.
It also quoted BA chief executive Robert Ayling saying the company would cut short-haul flights at Heathrow and move services to Gatwick, London's second airport.
The BA spokeswoman said it was too early to say which routes BA would chop to comply with the conditions laid down by the government for the merger with AA.
"We will look across the businesses and see which ones it makes most economic sense to lose," the spokeswoman said.
